topics.title: Logic Gates
notes: Logic gates are electronic circuits with one or more inputs and one output. Binary 1 and 0 are represented by voltage levels.
AND gate: output is 1 only when ALL inputs are 1. Expression: Y = A.B.
OR gate: output is 1 when ANY input is 1. Expression: Y = A + B.
NOT gate (inverter): output is the complement of the input. Expression: Y = A'.
NAND = NOT + AND: output is 0 only when all inputs are 1. NOR = NOT + OR: output is 0 when any input is 1.
XOR (Ex-OR): output is 1 when the two inputs are at opposite levels. Y = A XOR B = A'B + AB'. For 3 inputs, XOR gives 1 when the number of 1s is odd.
XNOR (Ex-NOR) = XOR + NOT: output is 1 when inputs are equal. For 3 inputs, XNOR gives 1 when the number of 1s is even.
NAND and NOR are universal gates: any gate (AND, OR, NOT) can be built using only NAND or only NOR.

topics.title: Boolean Algebra & Laws
notes: Boolean algebra deals with binary variables and the three basic operations AND, OR and complement. A Boolean function can be shown as a truth table, logic diagram or algebraic expression.
Commutative law: A + B = B + A and A.B = B.A (order of variables does not change output).
Associative law: (A + B) + C = A + (B + C); (A.B).C = A.(B.C).
Distributive law: A.(B + C) = A.B + A.C; A + BC = (A + B)(A + C).
Identity and null: A + 0 = A; A . 1 = A; A + 1 = 1; A . 0 = 0. Complement: A + A' = 1; A . A' = 0. Idempotent: A + A = A; A . A = A. Involution: (A')' = A. Absorption: A + AB = A.
De Morgan's theorems: (A.B)' = A' + B' (NAND becomes negative-OR); (A + B)' = A'.B' (NOR becomes negative-AND). Break the bar and change the sign.

Full list of postulates and theorems (slides): X+0=X; X+1=1; X+X=X; X+X'=1; X.0=0; X.1=X; X.X=X; X.X'=0; (X')'=X; X+Y=Y+X; X.Y=Y.X; X+(Y+Z)=(X+Y)+Z; X.(YZ)=(XY).Z; X+YZ=(X+Y)(X+Z); X.(Y+Z)=XY+XZ; X+XY=X; X(X+Y)=X.
Example from slides: F = x + y'z. F is 1 when x = 1, or when y = 0 and z = 1.

topics.title: Simplification using Karnaugh Map (K-map)
notes: K-map (Karnaugh map, also called Veitch diagram) is a method to minimize Boolean functions. It was developed by Maurice Karnaugh in 1954.
A minterm is a product term that includes all variables. Number of minterms = 2^n (2 variables: 4, 3 variables: 8, 4 variables: 16).
Each cell of a K-map represents one minterm. Values of variables are written in Gray code order (00, 01, 11, 10).

Rules: groups must contain only 1s; each 1 must be in at least one group; group sizes are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8, 16); make the largest possible groups; groups may overlap; groups may wrap around the table; groups must be horizontal, vertical or square/rectangular (not diagonal).
Sum of Products (SOP): use minterms (cells with 1). Product of Sum (POS): use maxterms (cells with 0).
3-variable K-map layout (Gray code): rows A = 0 and 1, columns BC = 00, 01, 11, 10. A=0 -> m0,m1,m3,m2; A=1 -> m4,m5,m7,m6.
4-variable K-map layout: rows AB and columns CD, both in Gray code (00, 01, 11, 10). Row 00 -> 0,1,3,2; row 01 -> 4,5,7,6; row 11 -> 12,13,15,14; row 10 -> 8,9,11,10.

Slide worked examples (SOP): F(X,Y)=Sum(2,3)=X. F(X,Y,Z)=Sum(0,4,6,7): correct minimal SOP is Y'Z' + XY (the slide shows XZ'+XY, which does not cover minterm 0). F(X,Y,Z)=Sum(1,3,6,7): correct minimal SOP is X'Z + XY (the slide shows YZ+XY, which does not cover minterm 1). Check these with your teacher.
Slide worked examples (POS): F(X,Y)=Pi(2,3)=X'. F(X,Y,Z)=Pi(1,3,5,7)=Z'. F(W,X,Y,Z)=Pi(0,4,8,12)=Y+Z.

topics.title: Combinational Circuits
notes: A combinational circuit combines logic gates. Its output depends ONLY on the present inputs. It has no memory.
A combinational circuit can have n inputs and m outputs.
Design steps: state the problem, assign symbols, make the truth table, obtain simplified Boolean functions, draw the logic diagram.
Examples: Half adder, Full adder, Half subtractor, Full subtractor, Parity generator, Parity checker, Multiplexer, Decoder, Encoder.
Half adder: adds two bits. Sum = X XOR Y, Carry = X.Y.
Full adder: adds three bits (X, Y, carry-in Z). Sum = X XOR Y XOR Z, Carry = XY + YZ + XZ (also written Z(X XOR Y) + XY).
Full adder carry can also be written as Carry = Z(X XOR Y) + XY.
Half adder truth table: X=0,Y=0 -> Sum 0, Carry 0; X=0,Y=1 -> Sum 1, Carry 0; X=1,Y=0 -> Sum 1, Carry 0; X=1,Y=1 -> Sum 0, Carry 1.
Full adder: sum is 1 for an odd number of 1s in X, Y, Z; carry is 1 when two or more inputs are 1.

topics.title: Flip-Flops
notes: A flip-flop is a binary cell that stores one bit. It has two stable states (0 and 1) and two outputs Q and Q' (complement).
Flip-flops are storage elements used in synchronous sequential circuits.
SR flip-flop: S = Set, R = Reset. S=0,R=0 holds; S=0,R=1 resets (Q=0); S=1,R=0 sets (Q=1); S=1,R=1 is an invalid/forbidden state.
D flip-flop (Delay/Data): output follows D at the clock edge, Q(next) = D. Simple, fast, used for registers and memory cells. Made by connecting R = D' and S = D.
JK flip-flop: J=0,K=0 holds; J=0,K=1 resets; J=1,K=0 sets; J=1,K=1 toggles. It has no invalid state.
T (Toggle) flip-flop: made by tying J and K together. When T=1 the output toggles on each clock; when T=0 it holds. Used in counters.
Applications: RS flip-flops in asynchronous counters and memory cells; D flip-flops in registers and counters; T flip-flops in counters.
Flip-flops are classified as Asynchronous and Synchronous. Types: SR, D, JK and T.
SR flip-flop truth table: S=0,R=0 -> No change; S=0,R=1 -> Reset (Q=0); S=1,R=0 -> Set (Q=1); S=1,R=1 -> Invalid. SR flip-flop can be built with two cross-coupled NOR gates.
D flip-flop truth table (clock edge): Clk=0 -> No change; Clk=1, D=0 -> Q becomes 0; Clk=1, D=1 -> Q becomes 1. Applications: memory cell, register, counter, synchronous system.
JK flip-flop truth table: J=0,K=0 -> No change; J=0,K=1 -> Clear (Q=0); J=1,K=0 -> Set (Q=1); J=1,K=1 -> complement Q(t)'.
T flip-flop: T=0 -> no change; T=1 -> toggle (complement). Slide table lists it with clock edges; standard convention: T=1 toggles the output on each clock.

topics.title: Sequential Circuits
notes: A sequential circuit output depends on present inputs AND past inputs (its state). It contains at least one memory element (flip-flop).
A sequential circuit = interconnection of flip-flops and gates.
Examples: Registers, Shift registers, Counters, Flip-flops.
Sequential circuits are harder to design and understand than combinational circuits.

mcq.q: Output of an AND gate is 1 when:
mcq.explanation: AND gives 1 only when every input is 1.

mcq.explanation: NAND = NOT + AND.

mcq.explanation: NAND and NOR are universal gates; any logic function can be built from NAND alone.

mcq.explanation: 3-input XOR is 1 for an odd number of 1s.

mcq.q: Output of a NOT gate for input 1 is:
mcq.explanation: NOT inverts its input, so 1 becomes 0.

mcq.explanation: Commutative law: changing the order of variables does not change the result.

short.q: Write the truth table of an XOR gate.
Why are NAND and NOR called universal gates?
short.answer: Any Boolean function (AND, OR, NOT) can be implemented using only NAND gates or only NOR gates.

short.q: What is the difference between an OR gate and an XOR gate?
short.answer: OR gives 1 when any input is 1 (including both). XOR gives 1 only when the inputs are different (opposite levels).

short.q: State the associative law of Boolean algebra.
short.answer: (A + B) + C = A + (B + C) and (A.B).C = A.(B.C). The grouping of operations does not change the result.

short.q: State De Morgan's theorems.
Simplify the Boolean expression A + A'B.
short.answer: A + A'B = (A + A')(A + B) = A + B.

short.q: Simplify the expression AC + ABC.
short.answer: AC + ABC = AC(1 + B) = AC.

short.q: How many minterms does a function of 2 variables have? Give the reason.
short.answer: 4, because 2^2 = 4 combinations of the variables (00, 01, 10, 11).

short.q: Write two rules for forming groups in a K-map.
short.answer: Groups must contain only 1s; group sizes must be powers of 2; groups may overlap and wrap around; groups must be horizontal, vertical or rectangular (not diagonal). (any two)

short.q: What is the difference between SOP and POS form?
short.answer: SOP (Sum of Products) is built from minterms (1 cells) as OR of AND terms. POS (Product of Sums) is built from maxterms (0 cells) as AND of OR terms.

short.q: What is a combinational circuit?
short.answer: A circuit made of logic gates whose output depends only on the present input combination and which has no memory.

short.q: Write the sum and carry expressions of a half adder.
short.answer: Sum = A XOR B (A'B + AB'); Carry = A.B.

short.q: Write the sum and carry expressions of a full adder.
short.answer: Sum = X XOR Y XOR Z; Carry = XY + YZ + XZ.

short.q: Name any four combinational circuits.
short.answer: Half adder, full adder, half subtractor, full subtractor, parity generator, parity checker, multiplexer, decoder, encoder (any four).

short.q: What is a flip-flop?
short.answer: A binary storage cell that stores one bit of information and has two stable states (0 and 1) with outputs Q and Q'.

short.q: Write the truth table of an SR flip-flop with S=1 and R=1 and say what is wrong with it.
short.answer: S=1, R=1 is an invalid (forbidden) state because the outputs are not defined; both outputs try to become the same value.

short.q: Explain the working of a JK flip-flop for J=1 and K=1.
short.answer: The JK flip-flop toggles: if Q was 0 it becomes 1, and if Q was 1 it becomes 0.

short.q: How is a T flip-flop made from a JK flip-flop and what does it do?
short.answer: Tie J and K together to make T. When T=1 the output toggles at each clock pulse; when T=0 it holds its value.

short.q: Give two applications of D flip-flops.
short.answer: Building registers, memory cells, counters (any two).

short.q: Give two applications of T flip-flops.
short.answer: Used in counters and in memory circuits to store data (any two).

short.q: Differentiate between combinational and sequential circuits.
short.answer: Combinational circuits have no memory and output depends only on present inputs. Sequential circuits have memory (flip-flops) and output depends on present inputs and past states.

short.q: Give two examples of sequential circuits.
short.answer: Registers, shift registers, counters, flip-flops (any two).
